deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a library loan slip, almost certainly from the Göttingen University Library, written in German Kurrent script. The three neighbouring pages are similar slips: the previous one requests Liouville's Journal, the next one Lamé's 'Leçons sur la théorie mathématique de l'élasticité des corps solides'.

Content, line by line:
(1) Ink: 'Poggendorff. Annalen der Physik und Chemie. | Dritte Reihe. Bd. 29'. The word 'Annalen' is underlined in red, probably by the librarian.
(2) Pencil, librarian's hand: '89'. This is very probably the running volume number. Poggendorff's Annalen were grouped in series of 30 volumes: series 1 is volumes 1–30, series 2 is 31–60, series 3 is 61–90. On that scheme, 'Dritte Reihe Bd. 29' is 60 + 29 = Bd. 89 (1853). The penciled '29' at the right repeats the series volume number.
(3) Ink: 'Tafeln zu dritte Reihe Bd. 1–3, 7–9, 10–12'. These are the plate volumes for series 3, vols. 1–3, 7–9 and 10–12, i.e. running Bde. 61–63 and 67–72 (about 1844–1847). Pencil strokes cross through parts of this entry, presumably marking items as checked out or returned.
(4) Large pencil note, librarian: most likely 'Zurückerhalten' ('received back'), possibly preceded by an initial. It cancels the loan.
(5) '46' in pencil is the archival folio number.
(6) Red ink: 'Febr. 25. 59.', the loan date, 25 February 1859.
(7) Ink signature: 'B. Riemann'. Below it is an abbreviated street or residence word; it is not securely legible and is perhaps a Göttingen street name.

Historical context, which is my inference: in early 1859 Riemann had just succeeded Dirichlet. He was working on mathematical physics problems that later produced 'Über die Fortpflanzung ebener Luftwellen von endlicher Schwingungsweite' (1860) and the fluid-ellipsoid paper (1861). He had earlier published in Poggendorff's Annalen himself (Nobili's rings, 1855). The slip documents his reading of the experimental physics literature, but it contains no derivation.

results.what: Library loan record: Riemann borrows Poggendorff's Annalen der Physik und Chemie, 3rd series vol. 29 (= running vol. 89), plus plate volumes for 3rd series vols. 1–3, 7–9, 10–12, on 25 Feb 1859.

deep.surprise_reason: A library borrowing slip with no mathematical content. It is of minor biographical interest only, documenting Riemann's consultation of Poggendorff's Annalen in February 1859, consistent with his known interest in physics.

checkable.asserts: With series of 30 volumes each, 3rd-series vol. 29 corresponds to running volume 89 (the pencil annotation).
The requested plate volumes (3rd series 1–3, 7–9, 10–12) correspond to running volumes 61–63 and 67–72.

transcription_corrections: The penciled '89' is not a mathematical quantity. It is the librarian's conversion of 'Dritte Reihe Bd. 29' to running volume number 89; the second penciled '29' at the right repeats the series volume.
'Tafeln zu dritter Reihe' (the 'Tafeln' are plate volumes); the ranges are '1-3, 7-9, 10-12', and some are crossed through in pencil.
The large pencil word is plausibly 'Zurückerhalten' (a librarian's return note), possibly preceded by an initial; the reading remains uncertain.
The red line 'Febr. 25. 59.' is the loan date (1859).
The word under 'B. Riemann' is an abbreviated address. It is not securely legible; 'Weststraße' is doubtful, and it may abbreviate a Göttingen street name.
